body: “It feels like there has been a certain pattern to United over the years since Fergie left in that there is usually a decent/good season usually achieving Champions League qualification followed by a drop-off the following season due to the additional games in Champions League and the defeats that usually come with that,” reckons John Brennan. “I’m thinking of 23-24 under Ten Haag, 21-22 under Solskjær and, going further back, 18-19 under Mourinho. If this pattern holds (and the results so far this season suggest that it might), I can see a draw tonight followed by a comfortable win for Man City at the weekend and all of a sudden Carrick is going to be under pressure.”

Thinking more about that United defence, this is a big evening for Leny Yoro. He was pretty good in his first season at Old Trafford, but didn’t get to play much last; ultimately, Carrick couldn’t afford to risk him because he had a formula that worked – Maguire and Martinez, plus fast counters – with points to win and a job to secure.

articles.title: World Rugby float plans for Six Nations match in US but England unlikely to participate
articles.summary: Governing body floating staging Ireland v Italy in US. World Rugby eyes commercial value in American fixtures. World Rugby wants a Six Nations match to be staged in the US and has offered financial incentives to the unions to do so – but England have effectively ruled themselves out on the grounds…
body: The US will stage the 2031 World Cup and World Rugby is seeking to capitalise commercially despite mounting fears over the parlous state of rugby union in the host country. As a result, the governing body is desperate to raise interest in the sport’s profile by staging high-profile matches Stateside, with Baltimore hosting the fourth Test between South Africa and New Zealand on Saturday.

A failed attempt was made to attract the British & Irish Lions to stop in Las Vegas on the way to Australia in 2025, though England did face the USA in Washington that summer while the All Blacks and Ireland met in Chicago last autumn. The 2030 finals weekend of the Nations Championship has also been slated for the United States.

Taking a Six Nations match to America would be an altogether more significant move given how financially valuable home championship fixtures can be to the competing unions. But World Rugby is willing to help bridge the shortfall and has floated Ireland v Italy as a potential fixture, given the number of expats from each country on the east coast.

articles.summary: Sussex off-spinner Jack Carson takes his 200th first-class wicket but half-centuries by Ryan Patel, Ben Foakes and Mahipal Lomror keep Surrey's heads above water at gloomy Hove.
body: A slow pitch offered little assistance to the Sussex attack but they will be satisfied that Surrey were never able to score at more than three runs an over on an attritional day.
Surrey finished day three on 294-7 - trailing by 99 - but with only a day left the game seems certain to end in a draw.
That would give Surrey more breathing space above the relegation zone and strengthen Sussex's ambition of at least emulating last season's fourth-place finish.

There were two moments when Sussex sensed an opportunity. They reduced Surrey to 47-3 when Ollie Pope, parachuted into the team after being left out of England's Test side at Edgbaston, was dismissed for just two.

articles.title: Glowing javelins and a $10m prize fund usher in a brave new world for track and field
articles.summary: The Ultimate Championship aims to revolutionise the sport with promises of bigger prize money and a greater role for athletes. Track and field’s brave new world begins in Budapest on Friday night.
body: It is all part of the new World Athletics Ultimate Championship, a three-day event with a prize fund of $10m which is designed to pit the best against the best, and kick off a minor revolution in the sport.

When Usain Bolt, who is a global ambassador for the event, was told that anyone who wins the 100m, 200m and mixed 4x100m relay here will walk away £250,000 richer, he smiled – and recalled a conversation he had just recently had with another legendary Jamaican sprinter, Asafa Powell.

“I was chatting to Asafa before I came here and we were like: ‘Jeez, we missed out on a big cash prize,’” he said. “I won a fair few championships and it still doesn’t add up to all that cash. I am sad I missed out on it, but I’m happy for the athletes.”

For years, the World Athletics president, Seb Coe, and chief executive, Jon Ridgeon, have wanted top athletes to earn money. But this is just the start of plans to make the sport richer – and more popular.

articles.title: ‘She’s buzzing’: Charley Hull to face world No 1 Nelly Korda in Solheim Cup opener
articles.summary: Hull will partner debutant Lottie Woad for Europe. USA seeking to retain trophy they won in 2024. Galleries at the 20th Solheim Cup have been granted a blockbuster start with Nelly Korda and Charley Hull to face off in Friday morning’s foursomes.
body: Hull will partner the Solheim Cup debutant Lottie Woad against the formidable USA pairing of Korda and Allisen Corpuz to begin the tournament. Nanna Koerstz Madsen and Céline Boutier will represent Europe in match two, where they will take on Alison Lee and Lauren Coughlin. Esther Henseleit and Leona Maguire have been selected for the hosts in the penultimate match, with Andrea Lee and Lindy Duncan in opposition. The foursomes will conclude with Europe’s Swedish duo of Maja Stark and Linn Grant facing Rose Zhang and Jennifer Kupcho.

“She’s been buzzing, she’s been so excited.” said Europe’s captain Anna Nordqvist of Hull. “Her and Lottie have got to play quite a bit on tour this year, so I think they were both very excited to be paired with each other.”

Angela Stanford, the USA captain, said Korda and Corpuz had “earned the right” to lead their team out. “I feel like if I didn’t put those two out, I would be questioned,” Stanford added. “I feel like the whole world knew that they were coming.”

articles.title: Roglic closes gap on Mas in Vuelta time trial
articles.summary: Primoz Roglic moves into second in the general classification and closes the gap on leader Enric Mas with a fourth-place finish in the time trial on stage 18 at the Vuelta a Espana.
body: The four-time Vuelta winner finished in a time of 35 minutes and 41 seconds to reduce the lead of Spaniard Mas, who came 12th, to one minute 37 seconds in the general classification.
Slovenian Roglic, who rides for Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe, overtook Felix Gall in the standings after the Austrian came home in 25th position, 1:36 slower than his podium rival.
Time trial specialist Stefan Kung of Switzerland won the 32.5km stage from El Puerto de Santa Maria to Jerez de la Frontera, three seconds ahead of Great Britain's Callum Thornley.
Compatriot Oscar Onley remains fifth in the general classification after finishing 17th, and he extended his lead over his rival for the young rider's white jersey Jacob Omrzel.

articles.title: Porsche Penske leadership speaks out on IMSA performance struggles
articles.summary: Thomas Laudenbach and Jonathan Diuguid addressed structural pace limits that have hampered PPM’s Porsche 963 to only one podium since dominating the opening two rounds
body: Porsche Penske Motorsport (PPM) leadership voiced strong frustrations over ongoing performance deficits during a media call on Thursday, targeting how the severe adjustments have hampered their campaign following a dominant start to the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship season.

After sweeping the opening two endurance rounds at the Rolex 24 At Daytona and Mobil 1 Twelve Hours of Sebring, PPM was hit with heavy Balance of Performance (BoP) mandates, pushing the Porsche 963 past the 1,100-kilogram mark for the first time in GTP/Hypercar history. Although the BoP evolves for each race weekend, the team has since scored just a single podium at Long Beach and currently suffers a four-race podium drought for both the #6 and #7 entries.

The pressure came to a head in the most recent GTP-headlined round at Road America, where Kevin Estre, piloting the #6 Porsche 963, collided with championship leader Jack Aitken’s #31 Action Express Racing Cadillac V-Series.R on the final restart while battling for second place. Both crashed out, and race officials placed Estre on probation for the remainder of the season.

articles.title: 49ers Down Under: ABC7 Eyewitness News in Melbourne for Niner's season opener against Rams
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers are Down Under to open their NFL season against the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, and ABC7 Eyewitness News will have complete coverage from Australia and the Bay Area. ABC7's J.R.
body: ABC7's J.R. Stone has arrived in Melbourne and will have live reports in the lead-up to the season opener and the latest on how 49ers fans are enjoying everything Australia has to offer.
Kangaroos, dingoes, wallabies, and of course koalas. All found in Australia and all found at Moonlit Sanctuary just outside of Melbourne.

"We flew in from California and when we think of Australia, we think of kangaroos and we think of koalas. What is it that has put them front and center that people love about these animals?" asked ABC 7's J.R. Stone.
"They are an iconic animal. They are only found in Australia, and look at them. They look cute and cuddly. They're cute, cuddly and look at those fluffy ears," said koala keeper Faye Hodgkinson.

articles.title: Russell: I have an answer to Antonelli's pace
articles.summary: George Russell insists he does "have an answer" to Kimi Antonelli's pace but admits he will need good fortune to catch his Mercedes team-mate at the top of the Drivers' Championship.
body: ​​​​​​Russell suffered a demoralising blow to his already faint title hopes at last weekend's Italian Grand Prix when he was beaten to victory by Antonelli despite the 20-year-old having started from 19th on the grid after receiving a penalty for exceeding his engine-part allowance.
The result saw Russell, who had started second in Monza, fall 66 points behind Antonelli with 10 rounds remaining, starting with this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid.
Russell started the season as the clear title favourite but has won just two grands prix compared to Antonelli's seven, with the Italian being consistently quicker, especially in terms of race pace.
Asked about finding himself in situation where he doesn't have an answer to Antonelli's speed, Russell replied: "I do have an answer and I'm working on it, and it's been much improved.

articles.title: Joshua's driver in fatal car crash has trial adjourned
articles.summary: The trial of Adeniyi Mobolaji Kayode, the driver involved in the crash that injured boxer Anthony Joshua and killed two members of his team, has been adjourned until November 17.
body: The case, which began in January at a magistrate court in Ogun State, was adjourned from September 10 as proceedings continued over charges arising from the fatal crash on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway.
Joshua's personal trainer, Latif Ayodele, and strength and conditioning coach, Sina Ghami, were killed.

Kayode faces charges including dangerous driving causing death, reckless and negligent driving, driving without due care and attention, and operating a vehicle without a valid national driver's licence.
Prosecutors allege that Kayode was attempting to overtake another vehicle when the SUV carrying Joshua and his team crashed into a stationary truck.
